title: Securities Trading Policy (GMD-CORP-POL-1004)

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Persons with authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the Company (any director, executive or otherwise, and other Key Management Personnel as set out in the latest Annual Report), Senior Employees of the Group, Key Consultants or Key Contractors, any other person designated as a Restricted Person by the Board in writing, and Connected Persons of any of them. Sections 4 to 7 (blackouts, clearance, speculative trading, protection arrangements, margin loans) apply only to this tier.

tiers.name: Managing Director & CEO, or any Executive Director
tiers.description: Executive directors including the Managing Director & CEO; a component of Restricted Persons distinguished only by their Approving Officer (the Chair) and by the Director notification obligations in Section 8.

tiers.name: Chair
tiers.description: The Chair of the Board; a component of Restricted Persons whose Approving Officer is the Managing Director & CEO.

tiers.name: Non-Executive Director (excluding the Chair)
tiers.description: Non-executive directors other than the Chair; cleared by the Managing Director & CEO and Chair jointly in consultation with one another.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel (excluding any Director), 'C-suite' Executives, General Managers and Company Secretary
tiers.description: Non-director KMP as named in the latest Annual Report, C-suite executives, general managers and the Company Secretary; cleared by the Managing Director & CEO. Should also inform the Chair or Managing Director of an intention to trade, copied to the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Group Managers, 'Heads of' function, Managers, members of the Group's Legal or Business Development teams and any other Restricted Person
tiers.description: Remaining Senior Employees and any other Restricted Person not covered by a higher row of the Section 6 table; cleared by the Company Secretary or Chief Financial Officer.

tiers.name: Key Consultant or Key Contractor
tiers.description: A key or senior contractor or consultant engaged by or providing services to the Group at the time. A Restricted Person, but expressly excluded from the Section 5.1 exception for exercising options or rights under a compliant employee incentive scheme during a Prohibited Period.

tiers.name: Connected Person
tiers.description: A spouse or partner, child or step-child under 18 years, a parent, an unlisted body corporate which the Restricted Person controls or is a director of, a trust of which the Restricted Person is a trustee and of which he or she or any of those persons is a beneficiary, or any other person over whom the Restricted Person has significant influence or control. A Connected Person is itself a Restricted Person.

definitions.hedging_definition: "protection arrangements" include transactions which: amount to "short selling" of Company Securities; operate to limit the economic risk of any Restricted Person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) including Company Securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under an incentive plan) on that Restricted Person's behalf; or otherwise enable a Restricted Person to profit from a decrease in the market price of securities.

windows.end_anchor: the end of the ASX trading session following the announcement to the ASX of the March quarterly report
the end of the ASX trading session following the announcement to the ASX of the annual financial accounts
the end of the ASX trading session following the announcement to the ASX of the September quarterly report
the end of the ASX trading session following the announcement to the ASX of the half-year financial accounts

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board (or its delegate) may impose an Additional Period from time to time, for example because the Company is considering matters that would require disclosure but for ASX Listing Rule 3.1A. It applies in addition to the Blackout Periods and is confidential: Restricted Persons must not disclose to anyone that an Additional Period is in effect.

rules.detail: Company Securities expressly include over-the-counter options, equity swaps, futures and hedges, whether cash settled or not, and Dealing expressly includes granting, accepting, acquiring, disposing, exercising or discharging an option or other right or obligation. Buying a put from a bank and writing a call to it are therefore each a Dealing in Company Securities: permitted outside Prohibited Periods with prior written clearance from the relevant Approving Officer. If the derivative is protective it must additionally clear Section 7.3.
rules.evidence: Company Securities means all securities issued by the Company, and includes shares, share rights, performance rights, options, and derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise.

rules.detail: Exchange-traded options, share warrants and similar instruments are named as prohibited where they are short term or speculative. A long-dated, non-speculative exchange-traded derivative is not caught by 7.2 and would fall back to being a Dealing requiring clearance, but the qualifier is applied by the Approving Officer together with the front page test.
rules.evidence: This prohibition includes short term direct dealing in Company Securities, including derivative market transactions involving exchange-trade options, share warrants, contracts for difference, and other similar instruments, which are short term or speculative.

rules.detail: Any derivative that operates as a protection arrangement over unvested Company Securities, or securities subject to a holding lock, is banned outright with no clearance route. Derivatives that are not protective remain Dealings requiring clearance.
rules.evidence: The entering into of all types of "protection arrangements" for any Company Securities: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: Absolute ban, at any time, on protection arrangements over unvested Company Securities; the definition reaches securities held beneficially on the Restricted Person's behalf, for example in trust or under an incentive plan. No Approving Officer discretion is available.
rules.evidence: The entering into of all types of "protection arrangements" for any Company Securities: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: Securities that have vested but remain subject to a holding lock or holding term (for example performance-based remuneration not yet released) are treated identically to unvested securities: protection arrangements over them are prohibited at any time. Release from the holding lock is itself an excluded dealing, after which the vested_unrestricted rule applies.
rules.evidence: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: For securities that are neither unvested nor subject to a holding lock, a protection arrangement is expressly permitted subject to approval under Section 6: prior written request to the relevant Approving Officer copied to the Company Secretary, written clearance valid five business days and withdrawable, outside Blackout Periods and any Additional Period, and satisfying the front page test.
rules.evidence: The entering into of all types of "protection arrangements" for any Company Securities: ... and otherwise, requires approval under Section 6.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A collar, prepaid forward or similar cash-out over vested unrestricted securities is a protection arrangement (it limits the economic risk of the holding) requiring approval under Section 6, and if it is secured on the securities the loan leg separately requires clearance under 7.4. Over unvested or holding-lock securities the same structure is prohibited outright.
rules.evidence: operate to limit the economic risk of any Restricted Person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) including Company Securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under an incentive plan) on that Restricted Person's behalf

rules.detail: Short selling is listed as a species of protection arrangement, so it is banned outright in respect of unvested or holding-lock securities.
rules.evidence: "protection arrangements" include transactions which: amount to "short selling" of Company Securities

rules.detail: Unusually, the policy does not ban short selling outright. Because it is drafted as a protection arrangement, short selling of securities that are not unvested or holding-locked 'otherwise requires approval under Section 6'. In practice a short sale would be speculative trading contrary to 7.2 and would fail the front page test, so clearance should not be expected.

Securities lending or borrowing is nowhere mentioned and is not within the Deal definition (applying for, acquiring or disposing; agreements to do so; granting or exercising options and rights). A stock loan that transferred title would be a disposal and so a Dealing, but the policy does not say so.

Contracts for difference are named in the speculative trading ban. The prohibition is qualified by the words 'which are short term or speculative', and a short CFD would independently be a protection arrangement enabling profit from a price decrease, prohibited over unvested or holding-lock securities and otherwise requiring Section 6 approval.
rules.evidence: This prohibition includes short term direct dealing in Company Securities, including derivative market transactions involving exchange-trade options, share warrants, contracts for difference, and other similar instruments, which are short term or speculative.

rules.detail: Margin loans are not banned; they require prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer under the Section 6 procedure. No vesting distinction is drawn in 7.4 itself, and a disposal resulting from the secured lender exercising its rights is an excluded dealing under 5.1.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer in accordance with the procedure set out in Section 6.

rules.detail: Granting security is not itself within the Deal definition, but taking Company Securities as collateral for any secured lending arrangement is expressly routed through Section 6 clearance. A charge or lien unconnected with lending is not addressed.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer

rules.detail: The clause is not confined to margin loans: 'or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities' captures a bank loan secured on collared shares. It is a clearance requirement, not a prohibition, and the Approving Officer may seek input from KMP and Senior Employees on reputational and governance implications before deciding.
rules.evidence: margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities

rules.detail: Qualitative ban with no stated holding period or matching window: short-term or speculative trading is prohibited 'under no circumstances', expressly extending to derivative market transactions that are short term or speculative.
rules.evidence: Under no circumstances should Restricted Persons engage in short-term or speculative trading in the Company's Securities.

clearance.tier: Managing Director & CEO, or any Executive Director
clearance.approver: Chair (or the holder of their delegated authority, failing which the Company Secretary)
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (details of changes in Company Securities held directly or indirectly)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: as soon as reasonably possible, to allow the Company to report within five business days of the change; directors must themselves notify the market operator within 14 days under s205G if the Company fails to do so
clearance.evidence: Restricted Persons must not Deal in Company Securities at any time (including in the exceptional circumstances referred to in Section 5.2) unless the Restricted Person first requests permission to Deal in writing (including email) from the relevant Approving Officer ... copied to the Company Secretary, and obtains a written response granting clearance to Deal

clearance.post_trade_deadline: as soon as reasonably possible (ASX reporting within five business days of the change)
clearance.evidence: Written clearance requested by: Chair — Approving Officer: Managing Director & CEO

clearance.approver: Managing Director & CEO and Chair, jointly in consultation with one another
clearance.post_trade_deadline: as soon as reasonably possible (ASX reporting within five business days of the change)
clearance.evidence: Non-Executive Director (excluding the Chair) — Managing Director & CEO and Chair, jointly in consultation with one another

clearance.tier: Key Management Personnel (excluding any Director), 'C-suite' Executives, General Managers and Company Secretary
clearance.post_trade_to: Chair or Managing Director, copied to the Company Secretary (notification of intention to trade, where possible)
clearance.evidence: where possible, other members of the KMP should inform the Chair or Managing Director of their intention to trade as permitted under this policy (copied to the Company Secretary)

clearance.tier: Group Managers, 'Heads of' function, Managers, members of the Group's Legal or Business Development teams and any other Restricted Person
clearance.approver: Company Secretary or Chief Financial Officer
clearance.evidence: Any written clearance granted under this policy will be valid for a period of five business days from the time which it is granted or such other period as may be determined by the Approving Officer.

carve_outs: Incomplete buy or sell orders placed outside a Prohibited Period may be completed within five trading days after the Prohibited Period commences, but cannot be varied and must be notified to the Company Secretary within 24 hours
short_term.evidence: Under no circumstances should Restricted Persons engage in short-term or speculative trading in the Company's Securities.

exceptions.evidence: transfers of Company Securities between a Restricted Person and their spouse, civil partner, child, step-child, family company, family trust or other close family member or of Company Securities already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Restricted Person is a beneficiary

an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in Company Securities) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party

exceptions.approver: the other trustees or the investment managers, acting independently of the Restricted Person
exceptions.evidence: where a Restricted Person is a trustee, trading in the Company Securities by that trust provided that the Restricted Person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a Prohibited Period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the Restricted Person
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer; a disposal of Company Securities arising from a scheme of arrangement

exceptions.approver: Board approves the plan determining the timing and structure of the offer
exceptions.evidence: trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders such as, a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board.
a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights (for example, under a margin lending arrangement)

exceptions.approver: Approving Officer (prior written clearance still required for the exercise or conversion)
exceptions.evidence: the exercise (but not the sale of Company Securities following exercise) of an option or right by a Restricted Person (excluding Key Consultants or Key Contractors) under an employee incentive scheme ... where: (i) the final date for the exercise ... falls during a Prohibited Period and the Company has been in an exceptionally long Prohibited Period ...; and (ii) the Restricted Person obtains prior written clearance

an acquisition of Company Securities under an employee incentive scheme; the vesting (but not the sale of Company Securities following the vesting) of Company Securities as a result of meeting performance hurdles, or release of Company Securities from holding lock or holding term in respect of Company Securities received by Restricted Persons as part of performance-based remuneration

exceptions.approver: Approving Officer (prior written clearance for the plan)
exceptions.evidence: trading under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided ... where: (i) the Restricted Person did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a Prohibited Period; and (ii) the trading plan does not permit the Restricted Person to exercise any influence or discretion over how, when, or whether to trade.

exceptions.approver: Approving Officer (Disposal Consent), on a written application with supporting documentation including accountant, bank and other independent institution contact details
exceptions.evidence: A Restricted Person, who is not in possession of Inside Information, may be given prior written clearance to dispose of or transfer (but not to acquire or otherwise Deal with) Company Securities during a Prohibited Period (Disposal Consent) ... where the person is in severe financial hardship

exceptions.approver: Approving Officer (Disposal Consent), on a written application with relevant court and/or supporting legal documentation
exceptions.evidence: A circumstance may be considered exceptional if the person in question is required by a court order or a court enforceable undertaking to transfer or sell, or accept a transfer of, the Company Securities or there is some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement for the person to do so.

financing.price_trigger_guidance: Incomplete buy or sell orders placed outside a Prohibited Period must be completed within five trading days once the Prohibited Period commences or they lapse, cannot be varied, and must be notified in writing to the Company Secretary within 24 hours of the Prohibited Period commencing.
financing_disclosure: Restricted Persons (all tiers); trigger: inception of any margin loan or other secured lending arrangement in relation to Company Securities; to the appropriate Approving Officer with a copy to the Company Secretary; deadline: before entering into the arrangement (prior written clearance)
All clearances are recorded: the Company Secretary maintains a register of notifications and clearances and must report them to the Board on request

external_documents: Latest Annual Report of the Company (identifies Key Management Personnel)
ASX Guidance Note 27 (Trading Policies) and the ASX Corporate Governance Principles and Recommendations, referenced as the source of the policy's requirements
exemption_authority: The Approving Officer determined under the Section 6 table may grant Disposal Consent during a Prohibited Period in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, court order or court enforceable undertaking, other overriding legal or regulatory requirement, or other circumstances deemed exceptional by the Approving Officer). That consent extends only to disposing of or transferring securities, expressly 'not to acquire or otherwise Deal with' them. There is no waiver power over the Section 7.3 ban on protection arrangements for unvested or holding-locked securities.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The entering into of all types of 'protection arrangements' for any Company Securities: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock; and otherwise, requires approval under Section 6.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the pivotal clause: a collar is permissible in principle over vested, lock-free shares with clearance, but is absolutely barred over unvested awards and vested shares still under a holding lock, so the collateral pool must be carefully segregated.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer in accordance with the procedure set out in Section 6.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike most ASX policies this does not ban secured financing, so the funded leg of the collar is available on approval, but the loan and the derivative legs each need clearance and both must be obtained before the structure is entered into.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights (for example, under a margin lending arrangement) [is excluded from the blackout restrictions] ... Unless otherwise stated, prior written clearance under Section 6 is not required for the above Dealings.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank can enforce its security and sell the collared shares during a Blackout Period or Additional Period without putting the executive in breach and without a fresh clearance, which materially de-risks the lending leg.

bespoke_clauses.clause: operate to limit the economic risk of any Restricted Person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) including Company Securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under an incentive plan) on that Restricted Person's behalf
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Shares sitting in an employee plan trust or a family trust count towards the hedging test, so a structure written over trust-held shares needs the same approval and, if those shares are still locked, is prohibited.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any written clearance granted under this policy will be valid for a period of five business days ... Written clearance under this policy may be withdrawn by the Approving Officer in writing at any time during the clearance period ... should the Approving Officer consider that circumstances have changed.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing, documenting and executing both the derivative and the loan must fit inside a five business day window that the Company can revoke at will, so the bank should expect signing risk up to the moment of execution.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Approving Officer may as appropriate, seek input from relevant Key Management Personnel and Senior Employees about the broader reputational, governance and other implications of the proposed Dealing ... Where any approval under this policy is required for a dealing, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the "front page" test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clearance for an executive collar is a discretionary reputational judgment rather than a mechanical check, and the front page test is an express bar on approval.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no acquisition relief in a blackout
bespoke_clauses.clause: may be given prior written clearance to dispose of or transfer (but not to acquire or otherwise Deal with) Company Securities during a Prohibited Period
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even in hardship, a collar cannot be entered, rolled or restructured during a Blackout or Additional Period; only outright disposals or transfers can be cleared, so timing must fall in an open window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Under no circumstances should Restricted Persons engage in short-term or speculative trading in the Company's Securities. This prohibition includes short term direct dealing ... involving exchange-trade options, share warrants, contracts for difference, and other similar instruments, which are short term or speculative.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A short-dated collar, or one with early termination or knock-out features, risks being characterised as short-term derivative dealing prohibited 'under no circumstances', so tenor and structure should be plainly long-term and protective.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person is: ... a Connected Person of any person referred to in the sub-paragraphs above.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A spouse, controlled company or family trust entering the collar or the loan is itself a Restricted Person needing its own clearance, so nothing is gained by moving the structure off the executive's own name.

bespoke_clauses.topic: OTC and cash-settled derivatives are securities
bespoke_clauses.clause: Company Securities ... includes ... derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cash-settled OTC collar cannot be argued to fall outside the policy on the basis that no shares move; it is a dealing in Company Securities in its own right.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company Secretary must maintain a register of notifications and clearances given in relation to trading in Company Securities ... and must report all notifications ... upon request by the Board.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any approval of a collar and secured loan will be recorded and reportable to the Board, and for directors the resulting change of interest is disclosed to ASX within five business days.

summary: A funded collar is possible for a Genesis Restricted Person, but only over Company Securities that are neither unvested nor subject to a holding lock, and only with two prior written clearances. Section 7.3 prohibits protection arrangements 'at any time' over unvested or holding-locked securities but otherwise routes them to Section 6 approval, and section 7.4 does not ban secured financing at all: margin loans and other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities simply require prior written clearance from the Approving Officer set by the Section 6 table (Chair for the MD & CEO and executive directors, MD & CEO for the Chair and non-director KMP, both jointly for other non-executive directors, Company Secretary or CFO for everyone else). Entry, roll or unwind must occur outside the four Blackout Periods running from 20 March, 20 June, 20 September and 20 December and outside any confidential Additional Period, must be executed within the five business days that clearance remains valid, and can be withdrawn at any time before execution on reputational or governance grounds or if it fails the front page test. Helpfully for the bank, a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights is an excluded dealing needing no clearance and permitted during a Prohibited Period, so enforcement does not breach the policy. The main structuring constraints are the ban on short-term or speculative derivative dealing in section 7.2, which argues for a long tenor and no speculative features, and the fact that hardship relief in a blackout extends only to disposals and never to entering a new arrangement.
